muller-lyer.name: Müller-Lyer Illusion
muller-lyer.author: Franz Carl Müller-Lyer (1889)
muller-lyer.source: Archiv für Physiologie (1889). Canonical geometric optical illusion.
muller-lyer.license: Public Domain. Canonical scientific benchmark illusion.
muller-lyer.question: Are horizontal lines A and B the same length?
muller-lyer.explanation: Both central horizontal line shafts are exactly 260 pixels long. The inward vs outward orientation of the tail fins produces a powerful perceptual illusion of differing lengths.

ebbinghaus.name: Ebbinghaus Illusion
ebbinghaus.author: Hermann Ebbinghaus (1902) / Edward Titchener (1901)
ebbinghaus.source: Grundzüge der Psychologie (1902). Canonical size-contrast illusion.
ebbinghaus.license: Public Domain. Canonical scientific benchmark illusion.
ebbinghaus.question: Are the two orange center circles the same size?
ebbinghaus.explanation: Both central orange circles have an identical diameter of 60 pixels. The size contrast of the surrounding inducers causes Circle A to appear smaller than Circle B.

ponzo.name: Ponzo Illusion
ponzo.author: Mario Ponzo (1911)
ponzo.source: Atti della Reale Accademia delle Scienze di Torino (1911). Canonical perspective illusion.
ponzo.license: Public Domain. Canonical scientific benchmark illusion.
ponzo.question: Are horizontal bars A and B the same length?
ponzo.explanation: Both yellow horizontal bars are exactly 130 pixels long. The linear perspective created by the converging rails induces an illusion that Bar A is larger.

simultaneous-contrast.name: Simultaneous Contrast Illusion
simultaneous-contrast.author: Michel Eugène Chevreul (1839)
simultaneous-contrast.source: De la loi du contraste simultané des couleurs (1839). Canonical brightness contrast illusion.
simultaneous-contrast.license: Public Domain. Canonical scientific benchmark illusion.
simultaneous-contrast.question: Are squares A and B the same shade of grey?
simultaneous-contrast.explanation: Both Square A and Square B have the exact same RGB color (130, 130, 130). Lateral inhibition causes Square A to appear significantly lighter against its dark surround.

cafe-wall.name: Café Wall Illusion
cafe-wall.author: Richard Gregory and Priscilla Heard (1979)
cafe-wall.source: Border locking and the Café Wall illusion, Perception 8(4), 1979.
cafe-wall.license: Public Domain. Canonical geometric optical illusion.
cafe-wall.question: Are the horizontal mortar lines dividing the rows parallel?
cafe-wall.explanation: Every horizontal grey mortar line is perfectly horizontal and parallel (slope = 0.0). The staggered black and white tiles create luminance border-locking signals that mislead human edge detectors.
